flap_deflection_deg.soft_note: Deflections above roughly 8 degrees add control authority but become increasingly separation-prone in this simplified 2D flap model.

hinge_gap_m.soft_note: A small hinge gap can relieve loading; excessive gap leaks momentum and increases wake loss.

flap_chord_fraction.soft_note: Very short flaps have weak authority; very long flaps can over-load the aft section.

blend_radius_m.soft_note: The blend radius softens hinge curvature. It must stay small relative to flap length.

engineering_notes: Useful designs trade control authority against drag and separation risk rather than maximizing flap deflection.
The hidden cases stay inside the disclosed speed, trim-bias, Reynolds, and submergence ranges.
No ranked public candidates, public scores, hidden anchors, or oracle geometry are disclosed.
A conservative template copy should be treated as a schema smoke test, not as an optimized hydrofoil flap design.
Use the public bounds, calibration samples, and transfer guidance to reason about authority, drag risk, separation risk, wake loss, and robustness before finalizing the design.

The public_transfer_guidance.json file gives public off-design regime descriptions and broad acceptable bands so hidden robustness is estimable without exposing private coefficient targets or duplicating private case keys.
Public calibration samples and transfer guidance are broad engineering aids. They are not hidden scores and do not identify a single official design.

coarse_design_guidance.purpose: Broad public guidance for honest exploration. These bands give coarse feasibility and tradeoff guidance; they do not publish coefficient windows or a hidden scoring target surface.
coarse_design_guidance.note: Strong candidates usually use moderate deflection, enough flap chord for authority, a controlled hinge gap, and a nonzero blend radius to delay separation. Excessive deflection or over-blockage can hurt drag and wake uniformity.
coarse_design_guidance.useful_performance_note: Public guidance, calibration windows, and transfer cases help avoid low-authority or over-aggressive designs and can earn meaningful partial credit. Exact high-credit coefficient anchors are private.
coarse_design_guidance.nominal_lift_authority_hint: Moderate designs should usually improve lift authority over neutral/template behavior. Exact coefficient anchors and high-credit windows remain private.

public_validation_case.note: Small public operating point for broad design reasoning. Hidden coefficient targets remain private.
